I’ll model the machine as a probability process, tracking every ball’s chance of being directly struck rather than discarded. I’ll first compute the distribution under the natural end-of-ramp convention (remaining balls are processed until none remain), then verify the maximizing label.
The state transitions are finite and can be evaluated exactly with probability mass propagation; no web or document lookup is relevant to this self-contained riddle.
There is no named document or institutional topic here, so I’m checking the permanent knowledge base only as required; the riddle itself should then be solved computationally.
```python
knowledge_check = await knowledge_search_knowledge("ping-pong ball game machine riddle", scope="all")
print(knowledge_check)
```
I’m now propagating all reachable machine states, including the final partial platform after ball 100 enters. The output will report the highest-probability ball and the probability profile around it.
The key invariant is that balls entering at the third position have identical future odds; only the initially placed balls have different starting positions. I’m checking the resulting position-based probabilities before selecting the earliest optimal label.
```python
odds_check = await calculator("1/3 + (1/3)*(5/9) + (1/3)*(1/3)")
print(odds_check)
```
3 (tied with every ball from 4 through 100)
